query: FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloys are promising bond-coat candidates because of their mechanical properties and elevated-temperature oxidation resistance. Earlier HVAF-M3 work identified 15–45 μm feedstock as optimal for high-quality coatings, but applying the same composition and size range with the HVAF-i7 torch yielded acceptable coating quality yet inadequate thickness. Separate studies of conventional MCrAlY bond coats using the M3 system reported a slight gain in deposition efficiency at higher particle velocity and nozzle-specific best spray distances of 300 and 350 mm. The design target is a sufficiently thick, adherent bond coat that retains coating integrity, minimal as-sprayed oxidation, and durability during high-temperature thermal-barrier service, including deposition within internal diameters as small as 120 mm. What single intervention could overcome the thickness limitation? State the hypothesized intervention and mechanism, predict the outcome relative to the 15–45 μm-feedstock baseline, define the deposition and service conditions under which it should remain effective, identify supporting evidence from the cited prior studies, and propose a controlled experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Reducing the spray distance during HVAF-i7 processing (to around 300 mm) increases particle velocity and deposition efficiency so that the resulting FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy bond coat is thicker while maintaining integrity and low oxidation.
generation.material_initial_state: FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy feedstock of 15–45 μm used in HVAF-i7 spraying that produces coatings with acceptable quality but inadequate thickness.
generation.intervention: Adjust the HVAF-i7 torch spray distance to an optimal value (approximately 300 mm) to boost the particle velocity at impact.
generation.conditions: Deposition in a HVAF-i7 setup for high-temperature thermal barrier service, including application in confined geometries (internal diameters as small as 120 mm); all other process parameters remain controlled and constant.
generation.structural_mediator: Enhanced particle impact kinetic energy leading to better splat formation and higher build-up of material on the substrate.
generation.mechanism: A shorter spray distance increases the velocity of the particles during flight, which improves their substrate impact, thereby increasing deposition efficiency and coating thickness without substantially raising as-sprayed oxidation.
generation.predicted_outcome: An increase in coating thickness relative to the baseline obtained with the standard HVAF-i7 settings, while retaining appropriate adhesion and minimal oxidation.
generation.baseline: Coatings deposited using the 15–45 μm feedstock with the original HVAF-i7 process parameters that yield acceptable quality but insufficient thickness.
generation.boundary: The intervention should remain effective under HVAF-i7 deposition conditions and during elevated-temperature thermal-barrier service, even when applied inside small internal diameters (≈120 mm).
generation.uncertainty: The precise magnitude of thickness improvement is uncertain and will likely depend on fine-tuning the spray distance and any related process modifications.

falsification_experiment.design: Conduct a controlled experiment where two sets of identical substrates are coated with the FeCoNiCrAl alloy using the HVAF-i7 torch: one set using the conventional spray distance (baseline) and the other set using a reduced spray distance of approximately 300 mm. All other parameters (e.g., feedstock size, composition, gas flows, temperature) are held constant. After deposition, measure coating thickness, adhesion, and oxidation levels.
measurements: Coating thickness (quantitative measurement across deposited samples)
Oxidation level (using surface analysis such as XPS or EDS)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the reduced spray distance does not result in a statistically significant increase in coating thickness (without compromising adhesion or increasing oxidation beyond acceptable limits) compared to the baseline, then the hypothesis is falsified.
